sentences.text: Hualianceratops was a small, herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur measuring about 1.2 meters in length with a skull approximately 25 centimeters long.
Its overall size was comparable to that of a spaniel.
The lower jaw featured a deep, short dentary bone holding at least seven teeth, while the upper jaw's maxilla contained at least nine teeth.
Unlike smooth bones of many dinosaurs, the skeleton of Hualianceratops possessed a unique texture, earning it the nickname 'ornamented dinosaur'.
As one of the earliest ceratopsians, this species lacked the prominent horns and frills typical of later relatives like Triceratops.
The species Hualianceratops wucaiwanensis was formally named in 2015 by Han Fenglu, Catherine A. Forster, James M. Clark, and Xu Xing.
The generic name merges Chinese characters for 'ornamental face' with the Greek word for 'hornface' to highlight the decorative patterns on its jaw bones.
The holotype fossil, which serves as the primary specimen for the species, was discovered in the upper Shishugou Formation.
In 2015, researchers placed Hualianceratops within the family Chaoyangsauridae.
This animal lived during the Oxfordian stage, a period spanning from 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago.
Living in western China, Hualianceratops was a vegetarian likely hunted by the tyrannosauroid dinosaur Guanlong.
Scientists have not yet resolved exactly how Hualianceratops relates to other members of its evolutionary clade.
